title: Smoking gene confounding and mediation readings
content: Figures 9.11 and 9.12 contain the same three arrows in different layouts. For the Smoking-to-Lung-Cancer question, Smoking Gene is a confounder. For the Smoking-Gene-to-Lung-Cancer question, Smoking is a mediator. The adjacent analysis reports an indirect effect of only 1 to 3 percent, CDE(0) essentially zero, and a strong gene effect among smokers; those empirical interaction claims are not structural equations.

variables.name: Smoking Gene
variables.content: The high-risk genetic variant associated with smoking behavior and lung cancer.

variables.name: Smoking
variables.content: Smoking behavior, read either as the exposure of interest or as a mediator of the gene's effect.
